data.name: Quasim
data.gender_notes: Quasim is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Quasimodo is a Latin word derived from the phrase quas immodus, meaning 'as much as is not moderate.' This name was popularized by Victor Hugo's novel 'The Hunchback of Notre Dame,' in which the protagonist Quasimodo is named after this term. The name Quasim carries the meaning “New or Fresh” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Quasim usually hope their child will grow to embody new or fresh and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A fresh start in life, a reminder to embrace change.
data.etymology: Quasim belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “New or Fresh.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Quasim total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: קוואזים
in_hebrew.meaning: כמו שנולדו - כמו שמתואר במעמד התחייה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קוואזים מקורו בלטינית ומשמעותו 'כמו שנולדו' או 'כמו שמתואר במעמד התחייה'. הוא מתאר את הרעיון של תחייה או לידה מחדש, ומשמש לעתים קרובות בהקשר של הטבילה הנוצרית ושם הילד שנולד מחדש בישו.

in_greek.name: Κουάζιμ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όρος Κουάζιμ προέρχεται από τη λατινική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'Όμοιος με εκείνον που αναστήθηκε' ή 'σαν να γεννήθηκε'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη και την πρώιμη Εκκλησία, το όνομα αυτό πιθανόν να συμβόλιζε την πνευματική αναγέννηση και τη νέα ζωή στον Χριστό.

in_latin.name: Quasim
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Quasim derivatum est ex latino et significat 'quasi natus' vel 'similis nato'. In traditione christiana, hoc nomen saepe ad baptismum et regenerationem spiritualem refertur, designans vitam novam et renasci in Christo.

in_english.name: Quasim
in_english.meaning: Similar to one risen; like one born
in_english.long_meaning: The name Quasim originates from Latin roots and translates to 'similar to one risen' or 'like one born'. Etymologically derived from quasi and natus, it signifies spiritual rebirth and renewal. Historically, Quasim is associated with the first Sunday after Easter in the Christian liturgical calendar, known as Quasimodo Geniti, reflecting themes of rebirth and new life in Christ. The name symbolizes spiritual regeneration and new beginnings.

data.cultural_impact: Quasimodo has become a cultural icon, synonymous with physical deformity, social outcasting, and the quest for human connection and love. The story of Quasimodo has elicited sympathy, empathy, and fascination among readers and audiences, challenging societal norms and broadening perspectives on the nature of beauty and the value of human life.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Quasimodo can be seen as a metaphor for the human condition, reminding us that all of us bear the weight of our unique burdens and imperfections. It also invites us to see beyond physical appearances and judge people by their character, acts of kindness, and their souls. In the spiritual context, Quasimodo's story can be seen as a call to love and accept others regardless of their appearances or perceived shortcomings. It serves as a reminder that true beauty lies within the heart and that everyone deserves love, respect, and compassion.
